:::{#thm-second-derivative-test}
#### Second derivative test

Let $c$ be a [flat point](#def-flat-point) of $f$ at which the [second derivative](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-second-derivative) $f''(c)$ exists.

- If $f''(c) > 0$, then $c$ is a strict local [minimum](algebra.qmd#def-minimum) of $f$.
- If $f''(c) < 0$, then $c$ is a strict local [maximum](algebra.qmd#def-maximum) of $f$.

If $f''(c) = 0$, the test does not decide.

The several-variable version for a minimum is @thm-second-order-condition.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: proof

Suppose $f''(c) > 0$.
Because $f'(c) = 0$, the [derivative](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-derivative) of $f'$ at $c$ is

$$f''(c) = \lim_{x \to c} \frac{f'(x)}{x - c}.$$

A limit that is positive forces the quotient to be positive near $c$.
So $f'(x)$ has the same sign as $x - c$ on some open interval around $c$.
Hence $f$ is decreasing to the left of $c$ and increasing to the right of $c$,
which makes $c$ a strict local minimum.

The case $f''(c) < 0$ follows by applying this argument to $-f$.

:::

:::
